newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai firm buys bankrupt firm in tender.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai firm buys bankrupt firm in tender.

text.p: A Shanghai company defeated a bid by a Shenzhen firm to take over a bankrupt alcohol factory in Shanghai,in the first such bid through public tender, the Liberation Daily said on Wednesday.

Guanshengyuan Collective Co Ltd of Shanghai paid 75 million yuan to take over the Shanghai Alcohol Factory, which was legally declared bankrupt in July with 680 workers, assets of 83.16 million yuan and debts of 350 million, a Guanshengyuan official said.
After the takeover, Guanshengyuan, a food producer, will not be responsible for the debts or the workers of the alcohol factory, he said.
The Liberation Daily said it was the first time a bankrupt state firm had been disposed of through a public tender, which was conducted through the Shanghai Property Assets Trading Centre.
The centre took responsibility for the disposal of the alcohol firm and announced that it would be sold by public tender, attracting the interest of nine companies, the newspaper said.
The centre evaluated the nine candidates and chose two for the final tender, Guanshengyuan and Shenzhen Laode New Power Investment Co Ltd, it said.
A panel of nine experts chose the Shanghai firm over the Shenzhen one, considering both the prices they were offering and other conditions of their bids, it said.

The Property Assets Trading Centre has 28 more bankrupt firms registered with it, waiting for buyers, and will dispose of them in a similar way, inviting bids from companies nationwide and from overseas, the newspaper said.
